SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Internal Telemetry, Routing Logs, & Interagency Code Enforcement (Ward 8)

To the District of Columbia Department of Buildings (DOB) FOIA Office:

Pursuant to the D.C. Freedom of Information Act, I am formally requesting internal email routing metadata, inspection dispatch logs, and internal communications regarding a known environmental and structural hazard located at the unaddressed retention basin adjacent to 2322 16th Street SE / Hunter Place SE (Ward 8).

This request specifically demands the following existing records:

1. EMAIL TELEMETRY & ROUTING LOGS: All internal routing metadata, server delivery logs, forwarding records, and help-desk ticket generation records associated with the email sent by DOB General Counsel Esther McGraw on August 26, 2026, at 9:34 AM to the intake address "dob@dc.gov" (Subject: "EMERGENCY HAZARD & CODE ENFORCEMENT NOTICE: Unsecured Stagnant Stormwater Basin & Public Nuisance"). 

2. ASSIGNMENT & INSPECTION RECORDS: All internal communications, code enforcement dispatch logs, inspection notes, and resulting Abatement or Stop Work Orders generated in response to the aforementioned August 26, 2026, email. 

3. INTERAGENCY COMMUNICATIONS: All emails, field notes, and communications between the Department of Buildings (DOB) and D.C. Health (DOH) regarding 311 Service Request #26-00509056. On August 26, 2026, at 9:57 AM, DOH Vector Control officially closed this service request by documenting: "In regards to the standing water that would be Department of buildings... regarding that issue." I am requesting all DOB records acknowledging or responding to this formal jurisdictional deferral from DOH.

BACKGROUND & JUSTIFICATION
On August 26, 2026, DOB General Counsel Esther McGraw explicitly stated in writing that she copied "dob@dc.gov" on my emergency notice and that "it will get routed accordingly for a response." I am requesting the digital paper trail proving where this email was routed and which enforcement officers were assigned to the case. 

FEE WAIVER REQUEST
I request a full fee waiver for this request. Disclosure of this information is strictly in the public interest, as it directly exposes potential systemic failures in the Department of Buildings' emergency intake systems and highlights severe municipal infrastructure neglect in Ward 8. The requester has no commercial interest in these records and operates as a community advocate. 

I look forward to your fulfillment of this request within the 15-day statutory deadline.

Please note that this FOIA request has been simultaneously uploaded to MuckRock.com for public indexing. Furthermore, the WUSA-9 investigative team is copied on this correspondence to ensure complete public transparency regarding the District's handling of known Ward 8 hazards.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock in Kennesaw
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the public records described below. The General Assembly has established a strong presumption that public records should be made available for public inspection and has directed that exceptions to disclosure be interpreted narrowly. O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70(a).

DATE RANGE
Unless otherwise stated, this request covers January 1, 2020 through the date this request is received. If the Department began using Flock Safety after January 1, 2020, this request covers the date of first use through the date this request is received.

RECORDS REQUESTED

1. Department search audit logs. All audit logs, search logs, and query histories generated by the Flock Safety platform (including exports available through the Insights or audit section of the Department's Flock administrative dashboard) for every search conducted by any Kennesaw Police Department user. Please include every field the platform or the Department maintains for each search, including but not limited to: date and time; user name, user ID, and badge or employee number; search type (plate, vehicle attribute, Nova, or any other search type); the reason or justification entered; offense or incident type selected; case, report, or CAD number entered; the time period searched; and the number of cameras, organizations, and networks searched.

2. Network audit logs. All audit logs showing searches of Kennesaw Police Department cameras or data by any outside agency or user, including every field maintained for each search, such as the searching agency, user identifier, date and time, search type, reason or justification entered, and case number.

3. Policies. All policies, general orders, standard operating procedures, directives, and memoranda governing the use of Flock Safety or any automated license plate recognition system, including every version in effect at any point during the date range.

4. Audits and oversight. All internal audits, supervisory reviews, compliance reports, and records generated by or in response to Flock's audit assistance tool or any other method of flagging searches, including records documenting how flagged searches were reviewed and resolved.

5. Misuse and discipline. All complaints, internal investigation files, and disciplinary records concerning alleged misuse of Flock Safety or any automated license plate recognition system, for investigations that have concluded. For any investigation still pending, please state that it exists and identify the specific exemption relied on.

6. Access and training. Records showing which Department personnel hold Flock user accounts and their access levels; all Flock training materials; and all user agreements, acknowledgment forms, or terms of use signed by Department personnel.

7. Contracts and data sharing. All contracts, statements of work, renewals, invoices, memoranda of understanding, and data sharing agreements relating to Flock Safety, and any record listing the agencies, organizations, or networks with which the Department shares Flock data or from which it receives access.

8. Communications with Flock Safety. All communications between the Department and Flock Safety concerning audit logs, changes to audit log content (including the removal of license plate numbers or officer names), audit tools, or public records requests.

9. Reports. All usage, statistical, or transparency reports concerning Flock Safety, including any transparency portal content and any reports or presentations provided to the Kennesaw City Council.

SCOPE AND O.C.G.A. § 35-1-22(f)
I am not requesting captured license plate data as defined in O.C.G.A. § 35-1-22(a)(2). I do not seek vehicle photographs, GPS coordinates of vehicle detections, or license plate numbers. If any responsive record contains such data, please redact only those specific values and produce the remainder of the record.

The records requested document the conduct of public employees: who accessed the system, when, and the justification they entered. A reason typed by an officer is a record of that officer's own action, not data captured by a camera. These records exist so that access can be reviewed for compliance with O.C.G.A. § 35-1-22(b), which permits access only for a law enforcement purpose. Numerous Georgia law enforcement agencies have released Flock audit logs under the Act.

PENDING INVESTIGATIONS
If the Department relies on O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(4) or any other exemption for particular log entries, please withhold only the specific entries or fields to which the exemption applies, produce all remaining entries, and state the number of entries withheld and the exemption applied to each category.

RECORDS HELD BY FLOCK SAFETY
Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70(b)(2), public records include data maintained by a private entity in the performance of a service or function for or on behalf of an agency. Records maintained on the Flock platform for the Department are therefore public records of the Department, whether stored on Department systems or by Flock Safety.

FORMAT
Please produce all records electronically. For audit logs and other data, please provide the native export format generated by the platform (CSV or XLSX), not PDFs or printed pages. Flock allows audit logs to be exported in consecutive increments, so the full date range can be produced by exporting successive periods.

TIMING
Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A), the Department must respond within three business days. If some records are available sooner than others, please produce them on a rolling basis. For any records not available within three business days, please provide a description of those records and a timeline for their production within that period.

WITHHOLDING
Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(d), any decision to withhold all or part of a record must identify the specific legal authority by code section, subsection, and paragraph. Where only part of a record is exempt, please redact the exempt portion and produce the rest.

FEES
Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c), any charges must be reasonable and may not exceed the hourly rate of the lowest paid employee capable of performing the work. Please provide a written, itemized estimate before incurring any costs exceeding $250.

PRESERVATION
Please preserve all responsive records, including audit logs subject to automatic retention limits, while this request is pending.

This request is made in writing so that the protections of O.C.G.A. §§ 50-18-73 and 50-18-74 apply. Thank you for your prompt attention.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Silence Dogood

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Enforcement and Complaint Records Concerning Hotels
communications.communication:
Dear Records Access Officer:

Under the New York Freedom of Information Law (Public Officers Law, Article 6), I request copies of the records described below. Unless a different period is stated, the period for each item is January 1, 2021 through the date this request is processed. Schedule A, below, lists the hotel addresses referred to in several items. Where an item refers to "a hotel," it means any hotel in Manhattan, including but not limited to those on Schedule A.

For any item that the Commission maintains in a database, case management system, or spreadsheet, an export of the responsive records from that system, with the fields identified in the item, satisfies the request. I am not asking for individual paper summonses or complaint forms where a system export exists. I have obtained 311 complaint data from NYC Open Data and am not requesting the 311 records themselves, except as stated in item 1.

Publicly available 311 data shows clusters of complaints in the category "Driver Complaint - Non Passenger" at the 58th Street entrance of the Four Seasons Hotel (32 East 58th Street, including eleven complaints filed on October 30, 2025), at 7 West 60th Street adjacent to the Mandarin Oriental, at the Park Lane Hotel (36 Central Park South), and at The New Yorker (481 Eighth Avenue), with dispositions indicating that the Commission issued notices, obtained guilty pleas, and scheduled OATH hearings. Several items below are intended to capture the complaint narratives, complainant types, summonses, and dispositions associated with those clusters. I have also received information that Commission enforcement personnel were present at the Four Seasons Hotel during the summer of 2026.

Records requested

1. Complaints received directly by the Commission, other than through 311, that reference a hotel, hotel doorman, hotel concierge, hotel bell staff, or a payment, tip, kickback, "vig," or commission paid by a driver, base, or for-hire vehicle company to hotel staff in connection with passenger referrals, airport trips, or vehicle dispatch, including complaints from passengers, drivers, and licensed bases. Fields: date received, complaint source or type, location, category, disposition. This item also includes, for any complaint whose incident location is a Schedule A address, whether received directly or referred from 311, the complaint narrative or description as recorded by the Commission and the complainant type (passenger, driver, base, hotel employee, or other) where recorded. 

2. Summonses and notices of violation issued for any incident located at a Schedule A address or within one block of it. Fields: date, incident location, rule or section cited, licensee type (driver, vehicle, or base), disposition. If the Commission's system does not support a proximity search, an export limited to incidents at the Schedule A addresses satisfies this item.

3. Decisions of the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, or of the Commission, resolving any summons or notice of violation responsive to item 2.

4. Records of any enforcement operation, detail, sweep, or undercover program conducted at or directed at a hotel from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including June through September 2026: operation plans, deployment orders, and after-action or results summaries, whether or not summonses were issued.

5. Records maintained by the Enforcement Bureau, including the Uniformed Services Bureau, reflecting the assignment or deployment of enforcement personnel at or to a hotel from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed, including tour or post assignment sheets, daily deployment plans, detail orders, and overtime authorizations that reference a hotel.

6. Any list, map, bulletin, briefing, or analysis maintained by the Enforcement Bureau or any intelligence, analytics, or planning unit that identifies hotels, hotel curbs, or "hot spots" for illegal solicitation, unlicensed pickups, or hustling in Manhattan, from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed.

7. Records showing the location of enforcement stops, summonses, or patrol posts at a Schedule A address from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including stop logs, summons geolocation data, and patrol or post lists.

8. Records of complaints or tips referred to the Enforcement Bureau for follow-up that reference a hotel, and the disposition of each referral.

9. Records showing whether any Schedule A address has been designated in the Commission's systems as an enforcement priority location, hot spot, or similar designation, and the date of each designation.

10. The Commission's 2026 driver survey described in the Commissioner's July 2026 letter to licensees: the survey instrument, the tabulated results, and any free-text responses that mention hotels, doormen, concierges, or solicitation or hustling at locations other than airports.

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the Presidential Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 2201 et seq.), I hereby request access to all textual records, visitor entry logs, protocol lists, and event rosters referring or relating to:

Günter Straßmeir (transliterations: Gunter Strassmeir, Gunter Strassmeier, Gunther Strassmeir; DOB: June 20, 1929 – DOD: December 24, 2009), former Parliamentary State Secretary to Chancellor Helmut Kohl and member of the Berlin House of Representatives. 

For guidance, here's the German Wikipedia entry: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCnter_Stra%C3%9Fmeir Strassmeir was a close confidant and former chief of staff to Helmut Kohl.
